fatal_errors: It substitutes untested plasma-facing service conditions, including high heat and neutron flux, for the reported quasi-static compression, indentation up to 500 °C, and room-temperature scratch tests.
The proposed comparison does not isolate the hypothesized effects of lattice distortion or grain-boundary cohesion.
The cited evidence supports only general motivation for tungsten and refractory high-entropy alloys, not the specific WTaTiVZr mechanism or predicted toughness and plasticity.
It omits the segregated two-BCC-phase dendritic microstructure that is central to the material state being evaluated.
explanation: The response captures the broad interpretation that multicomponent solid-solution strengthening and lattice distortion can preserve strength while Ti/V/Zr-related cohesion or deformation effects may improve plasticity and toughness relative to tungsten. However, it provides only a generic hypothesis and directional outcome. It does not reconstruct the as-cast, repeatedly remelted state, W-Ta-rich dendrites and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions, quantitative tungsten baseline, temperature-dependent transition in cracking, or scratch-toughness comparison. Most importantly, it presents irradiation and operating plasma-facing conditions as the test domain even though those conditions were not studied. Its falsification rule tests only whether the alloy is better, not whether the stated mechanism causes the improvement; composition-matched microstructural controls or direct dislocation, segregation, and crack-path measurements would be needed to discriminate the mechanism.
